Water.notes: Three things in this module do not match what the panel and the README promise. The chorus depth trimmer is configured and drawn but appears in no expression outside the widget, so it is dead (Water.cpp:41, 285). The three chorus LFOs are meant to be 120 and 240 degrees apart, but the offsets are written as std::sin(2*M_PI*(p - 120)) and (p - 240) at Water.cpp:187-193, and subtracting a whole number of cycles from a normalised phase leaves the three sines identical. The internal chorus feedback is multiplied by a variable passed into the delay function by value and never written back (Water.cpp:86-137), so it stays at zero. The module also declares a second output for testing the tremolo LFO which has no jack on the panel.

TripLFO.notes: The phase offsets are written as std::sin(radianPhase - 120) and (radianPhase - 240) at TripLFO.cpp:100 and 105. Those constants are radians, not degrees, so the spacing is 120 and 240 radians reduced into a cycle: roughly a tenth and a fifth of a cycle rather than the third and two-thirds the panel prints. The polyphonic output writes channels i, i+1 and i+2 inside the per-channel loop (TripLFO.cpp:114-116) while declaring three channels, so with a polyphonic rate cable the channels overwrite each other; with a monophonic rate jack it is correct.

LogProb.notes: The inverter output writes 5V rather than the 10V the three logic outputs use (LogProb.cpp:89). The two coin-toss results are single booleans shared by every channel (LogProb.cpp:32-33), so under polyphony the last channel's toss decides the result for all of them. The toss is taken by a BooleanTrigger fed the raw voltage (LogProb.cpp:60, 69), which counts any voltage other than zero as high, while the logic itself reads a gate as high only above 1V.
